items.prompt: Which memory is counted as auxiliary space?

options.text: Additional working storage used to compute the result, excluding pre-existing input and separately reported output.
Every byte occupied by the input.
Every required returned value.
The source-code text length.

feedback.reason: Auxiliary space describes extra working state created for computation.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Classify runtime storage before counting it. Caller-provided input already exists, and the required returned representation is reported as output space. Auxiliary space is the additional live state used to compute that output—temporary containers, indices, buffers, and active recursion frames.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.input_always: Caller-owned input is normally reported separately because the algorithm did not allocate it as working state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.output_always_aux: Storage required to represent the returned result belongs to output space unless the stated convention explicitly combines categories.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.code_size: The question concerns live runtime data, not the static number of characters in the source file.

items.prompt: A function creates many temporary arrays one after another, but frees each before creating the next. What determines peak auxiliary space?

options.text: The largest amount simultaneously alive, not the sum of all allocations over time.
The total number of bytes ever allocated.
Only the final allocation.
Only the number of variable names.

feedback.reason: Space complexity is a peak-concurrency measure.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Draw the allocation lifetimes on one timeline. Because each temporary is freed before the next begins, their sizes do not coexist; peak auxiliary space is the largest individual temporary plus any shared live state. Summing all allocations would measure allocation traffic, not maximum footprint.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sum_all_allocations: Released temporaries no longer occupy memory, so cumulative allocated bytes can greatly exceed the maximum live footprint.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.last_only: The final temporary determines the peak only if no earlier simultaneously live footprint was larger.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.variable_count: One variable can reference an n-element buffer while many scalar names remain constant-sized; names are not bytes.

items.prompt: An iterative algorithm uses ten scalar variables regardless of n. What is its auxiliary space?

options.text: O(n) because the variables process n inputs.
Impossible to classify without their names.

feedback.reason: A fixed number of fixed-size values does not scale with input size.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

At every point in execution, exactly ten fixed-size scalar slots are needed. Their count and width do not depend on n, so peak working storage is bounded by one constant: Θ(10) = Θ(1). Processing n inputs can take growing time without retaining n values.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.linear: The same ten slots are reused while processing the inputs; no additional scalar is retained for each element.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ten_n: Ten variables means Θ(10), not ten new variables per one of n inputs.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unknown: A fixed number of fixed-size scalars is sufficient information.

items.prompt: A recursive function has depth n and each frame stores O(1) local state. What stack space does recursion use?

options.text: O(n).
O(1) because each frame is constant-size.
O(n²) because recursion is nested.
O(log n).

feedback.reason: Peak stack memory equals active depth times per-frame storage.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

At maximum depth, n calls have not yet returned, so all n frames coexist on the stack. If each frame retains at most c bytes, peak stack use is n · c = Θ(n). Completed calls are irrelevant to the peak, but active depth is not.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.constant: Each frame is constant-sized, but n such frames coexist at the deepest point and their storage adds.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.quadratic: Constant frame size multiplied by depth n is linear.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.logarithmic: The prompt gives depth n rather than a halving recursion with depth log n.

items.prompt: A hash map stores one entry per distinct input value, and there are d distinct values. What parameter gives the tight auxiliary-space expression?

options.text: O(d).
O(n) only.
O(1) because each lookup is expected constant-time.
O(log d).

feedback.reason: Storage follows the number of retained keys.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The map retains one entry for each of d distinct values, so its live entry count is Θ(d). Because d ≤ n, O(n) is a valid looser worst-case expression, but O(d) states the storage driver directly and remains tighter when duplicates make d much smaller.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always_n: O(n) is a worst-case bound, but d is the tighter direct parameter.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.constant: Expected O(1) lookup time describes one operation and does not make a d-entry container constant-sized.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.log_d: A logarithmic expression would require only logarithmically many retained entries, but the map stores one for every distinct value.

items.prompt: A function returns a new array of k results and otherwise uses only two indices. Which classification is precise?

options.text: O(k) output space and O(1) auxiliary space.
O(k) auxiliary space and O(1) output space.
The same array counts as both output and auxiliary space.
Both are O(1) because only two indices are used.

feedback.reason: The result array is output storage, while the indices are working state.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The new list must contain k returned records, so it contributes Θ(k) output space. The two indices are the only additional working state and remain fixed in number, giving Θ(1) auxiliary space. Reporting the categories separately prevents the same result list from being counted twice.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.aux_k: Because the new array is the required returned representation, its k elements are output rather than temporary working storage.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.both_k: The same list has one semantic role here and should not be charged simultaneously as both output and auxiliary space.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_constant: Although the working indices are constant-sized, the returned list must retain k records and therefore grows with k.

items.prompt: A function sorts an input array in place using an implementation with O(log n) recursion depth. What auxiliary term must be included?

options.text: O(log n) recursion-stack space.
The input array itself as O(n) auxiliary space.
A mandatory new O(n) output array.
O(1) because the elements remain in the same array.

feedback.reason: In-place mutation can avoid a second array without eliminating call-stack storage.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

In-place means the element rearrangement reuses the input array rather than allocating a second n-element buffer. It does not make recursive control free: O(log n) active calls coexist, each with O(1) retained state, so their product contributes O(log n) auxiliary stack space.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.input_n_aux: The caller-provided array is the input being mutated, not an additional n-element working allocation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.output_n: An in-place sort returns or mutates the same array and does not require a new n-element output buffer.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.constant: The array allocation is reused, but logarithmically many active recursion frames still coexist.

items.prompt: Why does the total number of allocations not by itself determine space complexity?

options.text: Allocations may be released or reused, so peak simultaneously live memory is what matters.
Allocations never consume memory.
Only variable names determine memory.
Allocation count is always identical to running time.

feedback.reason: Space complexity is not cumulative allocation traffic.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Two executions can allocate the same total bytes yet have different peaks: one may free each buffer immediately, while another retains all buffers together. Space complexity follows the maximum sum of simultaneously live allocations, so allocation count must be combined with size and lifetime overlap.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.allocations_free: Every allocation consumes memory while live even if it is later released or reused.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.names_only: Variable names reveal neither the size of referenced storage nor how long different allocations overlap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.time_equals_space: Allocation activity can affect running time, but cumulative events and peak simultaneously live bytes are different measurements.

items.prompt: Which storage categories should be separated in a careful analysis? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pre-existing input storage.
Storage required to represent the returned result.
Temporary working memory and call-stack state.
The number of source-code lines.

feedback.reason: Space explanations should identify storage by semantic role.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

Input names the pre-existing representation, output names storage required by the result contract, and auxiliary names extra state used during computation. Keeping those roles separate shows what “in place” actually saves and prevents one structure from being charged in multiple categories.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.source_lines: Source formatting is static program text and is not a live data structure whose size follows the runtime input.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.input: Input storage can be reported for completeness but normally is not charged as newly allocated working memory.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.output: The result contract can force output storage even when the algorithm's internal working state is constant.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.auxiliary: Temporary containers, scalars, buffers, and active stack frames are the additional computational storage being optimized.

items.prompt: Which structures contribute to auxiliary space in a boolean duplicate detector? Select all that apply.

options.text: A seen set discarded after returning the boolean.
A constant number of indices or iterators.
The returned boolean as O(1) output space.
The caller-provided input array.

feedback.reason: Temporary state is auxiliary even when it stores input-derived values.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The seen set is created only to remember previously observed values and is discarded after the decision, so up to d retained keys are auxiliary state. Loop indices add O(1) auxiliary space. The caller's array remains input, and the one returned boolean is O(1) output rather than working storage.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.boolean_result: The boolean is the required returned representation and is classified as constant output space, not auxiliary state.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.input_array: The caller supplied the array before execution, so reading it does not make its n elements an auxiliary allocation.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.seen_set: The temporary set retains input-derived keys solely to support computation and can grow with the number of distinct values.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.loop_indices: A fixed number of indices is live during the scan and contributes a constant auxiliary term.

items.prompt: Which facts determine recursion-stack space? Select all that apply.

options.text: The maximum number of simultaneously active calls.
The asymptotic local storage retained by each frame.
The total number of calls over the whole execution.
The names of recursive functions.

feedback.reason: Peak recursive space is based on simultaneous frames, not cumulative call count.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

At the deepest point, `max_depth` frames coexist. If one frame retains S(n) local storage, their combined stack contribution is the sum across that active chain—often depth × frame size when frames are uniform. Calls that already returned no longer occupy stack space.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.total_calls: Total calls affects time, but sequentially completed calls release their frames and need not coexist at the memory peak.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.call_names: Function identifiers reveal neither maximum active depth nor the amount of local data retained in each frame.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.max_depth: Maximum active depth determines how many frame allocations coexist on the root-to-current-call chain.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.frame_size: Per-frame retained buffers or records are repeated across that active depth and can dominate stack space.

items.prompt: Which cases can have O(1) auxiliary space? Select all that apply.

options.text: An iterative in-place scan with a fixed number of scalars.
A streaming producer that emits results without retaining them and uses fixed local state.
A constant number of fixed-width masks.
A recursion of depth n with one frame per level.

feedback.reason: Auxiliary space depends on retained working state.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

An in-place scan reuses input and keeps fixed scalars; a streaming producer releases or emits each result rather than retaining the whole output internally; and a constant number of fixed-width masks occupies fixed storage. Each therefore keeps simultaneously live working state bounded independently of n.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recursive_depth_n: One constant-sized frame at each of n active levels yields Θ(n) stack space, not O(1).

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.in_place_scan: Reusing the input plus a fixed number of scalar indices keeps extra working storage constant.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.stream_output: A producer can emit arbitrarily many results while retaining only the current item and fixed control state.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.fixed_word_mask: A constant number of masks has fixed storage only under the explicitly fixed-width word model.

items.prompt: Arrange the process for deriving space complexity.

elements.text: List input, output, temporary structures, and recursion frames.
Determine the maximum simultaneously live size of each auxiliary component.
Add concurrent terms and simplify the dominant asymptotic bound.

feedback.reason: A space proof must account for both role and lifetime.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

items: List every material runtime store: input, required output, temporary containers, scalars, and active recursion frames.
Assign each store one semantic role so input and output are not double-counted as auxiliary memory.
For every auxiliary component, determine its maximum live size and which other components coexist with it.
Add simultaneously live terms, take maxima across non-overlapping phases, and simplify the resulting peak bound.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: Arrange the analysis of recursive stack space.

elements.text: Multiply depth by asymptotic per-frame size when frames coexist.
Add other simultaneously live auxiliary structures.

feedback.reason: Recursive space follows concurrent frames and their retained state.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

items: Derive the maximum number of calls simultaneously active on one recursion path.
Determine what local data each active frame retains while its child runs.
Sum frame sizes along the active path, or multiply depth by a uniform asymptotic frame size.
Add other auxiliary structures that coexist at that deepest point, then report the dominant peak term.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: Arrange the comparison of two sequential temporary buffers.

elements.text: Determine the size of the first buffer.
Confirm it is released before the second buffer is allocated.
Use the maximum rather than the sum for peak auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Non-overlapping lifetimes do not contribute simultaneously.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

items: Measure the maximum live size A(n) of the first temporary buffer.
Verify that its lifetime ends before allocation of the second buffer begins.
Measure the second buffer's maximum live size B(n) and any shared state S(n).
Because the buffers never coexist, report `max(A(n), B(n)) + S(n)` rather than `A(n) + B(n) + S(n)`.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: An iterative scan uses three indices and returns no growing result. Select auxiliary-space complexity.
constraints: All scalar values have fixed size.

feedback.reason: A fixed number of fixed-size scalars does not grow with n.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

All three indices coexist, but their count is fixed: peak working state is three machine-word values plus constant control state. Increasing n changes how long the scan runs and the values stored in the indices, not how many index slots exist, so auxiliary space is Θ(1).

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: A recursive function has depth n and stores an O(1) record in each active frame. Select auxiliary-space complexity.
constraints: No other growing structure is used.

feedback.reason: n constant-size frames coexist at maximum depth.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

At maximum depth, n calls are simultaneously waiting for their child to return. If each frame retains at most c bytes, stack space is n · c = Θ(n). The total number of calls is not the calculation; the active chain is.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: A divide-and-conquer recursion has depth O(log n), and every active frame stores O(1) local state. Select stack-space complexity.
constraints: Child calls are processed depth-first rather than retained simultaneously as full subtrees.

feedback.reason: Only one root-to-leaf chain is active in depth-first recursion.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

A depth-first evaluation completes one child before moving to another, so sibling subtrees do not keep their full stacks simultaneously. The active root-to-leaf chain has O(log n) frames, each retaining O(1) state, giving O(log n) stack space.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: A function builds an n by n boolean table and returns one scalar result. Select auxiliary-space and output-space complexity.
constraints: The table is discarded before return.

feedback.reason: The table is temporary working storage, while the result is constant-size.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The table contains n rows with n boolean cells each, so it retains n · n = Θ(n²) temporary cells and is auxiliary storage. The function returns one scalar regardless of n, so output space is Θ(1). These categories are reported separately even though both are live near return.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.

items.prompt: A function returns k matched records in a new list and uses a hash set containing d temporary keys. Select auxiliary-space and output-space complexity.
constraints: The hash set is not returned.

feedback.reason: The temporary set and returned list have separate roles and parameters.

blocks.text: How to reason about it

The hash set retains d temporary keys solely to compute matches, so auxiliary space is Θ(d). The returned list must retain k records required by the result contract, so output space is Θ(k). If total live memory were requested, their overlap could yield Θ(d + k), but neither category should absorb the other.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: For space, classify storage by role and count what is live at the same time. Total allocation traffic and peak auxiliary memory are different measurements.
